trigger: two DIFFERENT per-device definitions dispatched via workflow steps (which share the literal empty string as execution_id for every definition), overlapping target agent, one succeeds and stays genuinely open, the other's send fails or is quarantined
summary: release_concurrency_claim(s) and renew_concurrency_claim matched only (execution_id, agent_id), with no definition_id predicate -- the table's actual uniqueness key is (definition_id, agent_id), so an unscoped release for one definition's failed/quarantined send could release a DIFFERENT, still-genuinely-open definition's claim on the same agent, admitting a real concurrent duplicate dispatch. Traced through workflow_routes.cpp's dispatch_fn (every workflow-step dispatch passes execution_id='') and wire_and_dispatch_confined's not_sent/denied_quarantined fast-release call. Not reproduced against live Postgres by the reporting agent, but traced end-to-end through real code with no gaps.
classification_rationale: missing WHERE-clause predicate; the claim table's real uniqueness key was not the key used to scope the mutation
caused_by: 922a05c5d (original ADR-1007 implementation) -- present since the release/renew functions were first written, not introduced by a later round
waiver_rationale: Fixed: release_concurrency_claim, release_concurrency_claims, and renew_concurrency_claim now all require definition_id in their WHERE clause. The fast-release call site (dispatch_scope_ladder.hpp) already had definition_id in scope -- direct parameter-threading fix. The terminal-response path (update_agent_status) gained a new indexed PK lookup (definition_id_for_execution), fired only on a terminal/running transition, not per poll. That specific caller was never actually exploitable (a real execution_id is globally unique and 1:1 with exactly one definition_id by construction, and notify_exec_tracker already refuses to call update_agent_status when execution_id is empty) -- fixed anyway for API consistency and defense-in-depth. Regression test added: test_execution_tracker.cpp 'release_concurrency_claim/s do NOT cross-release a different definition's open claim when execution_id collides'. Full trace and fix description: docs/adr/1007-concurrency-enforcement-scope.md's new 'CLOSED: the shared empty execution_id...' section.

trigger: an agent never sends a terminal response but keeps sending non-terminal 'running'/keepalive signals indefinitely (stuck, buggy, or malicious agent)
summary: renew_concurrency_claim has no absolute ceiling on total claim lifetime independent of the rolling TTL -- a claim can be renewed forever, indefinitely blocking re-dispatch of that one definition to that one device. Scoped impact (one device+definition pair, not fleet-wide), MEDIUM not HIGH.
classification_rationale: missing a defensive bound, not a contract violation
waiver_rationale: Deferred: a max-renewals or max-age-since-claimed cap independent of the rolling TTL is a real hardening item but not required to close this PR -- the blast radius is bounded to one (definition, agent) pair, and the existing reconciler + TTL renewal design is documented as the accepted mechanism. To be filed as a follow-up issue per the governance post-run procedure.

trigger: an operator reading the changelog fragment for the DirectorySync 409 change
summary: Changelog fragment claimed 'previously 500' for POST /api/directory/sync's concurrent-call race, in the same sentence as 'silently allowed' -- self-contradictory, and git show against the merge-base confirms the old sync_entra had no re-entrancy guard at all (a race would interleave writes, not deterministically return 500). Every other doc (ADR, upgrading.md, rest-api.md) correctly described this as racing/interleaving.
classification_rationale: factually imprecise characterization of pre-fix behavior, not a truth contradiction about the shipped fix itself
waiver_rationale: Fixed: replaced '(previously 500)' with an accurate description ('previously: no guard at all -- two concurrent calls could interleave writes with no error').

trigger: an operator or integrator reading the 3xxx orchestration error-code table in any of the three docs to understand what a given code means
summary: The 3xxx orchestration error-code tables in yaml-dsl-spec.md, Instruction-Engine.md, and user-manual/instructions.md carried stale ORCH_* names (ORCH_EXPIRED/ORCH_AGENT_MISSING/ORCH_APPROVAL_REQUIRED/ORCH_CANCELLED) with WRONG meanings, not just wrong names -- none of those strings exist anywhere in the codebase (grep confirms zero hits); the real registered constants (error_codes.hpp/.cpp) are kDefinitionNotFound(3001)/kApprovalRequired(3002)/kScopeEmpty(3004)/kScheduleExpired(3005), and this PR's own 3003 row (ConcurrencyBlocked) already used the correct bare registered name style, leaving the adjacent rows inconsistent. This PR edited the adjacent 3003 row in all three tables while leaving the wrong rows untouched -- pre-existing defect this PR's own scope should have caught given it touched the same tables.
classification_rationale: documented error-code meanings did not match the actual registered taxonomy -- a truth defect per standing rule 3, not merely stale wording
waiver_rationale: Fixed: all three tables' 3001/3002/3004/3005 rows corrected to the real registered names and meanings, with an added note that (like 3003) none of them currently has a production call site emitting them. Wider table naming-convention inconsistency (1xxx/2xxx/4xxx rows also use a stylized SCREAMING_SNAKE convention that doesn't match error_codes.cpp's bare names) noted but NOT fixed here -- those rows are untouched by this PR's diff, out of proportion to fix in this fix round; worth a dedicated follow-up.

trigger: an operator debugging unexpected agent-to-server network chatter on a large fleet after upgrading to this release
summary: upgrading.md's new keepalive section never states the 5-minute interval or that it's new empty-payload gRPC wire traffic per in-flight command.
classification_rationale: reasonable omission (the mechanism is intercepted before touching SSE/dashboard/metrics by design) but a pointer would help an operator investigating wire volume
waiver_rationale: Fixed: added a sentence stating the 5-minute interval and per-in-flight-command empty-frame nature of the keepalive traffic.

trigger: a reader of the ADR's metrics section trying to confirm which counters are pre-seeded vs describe-only
summary: ADR stated 'the three counters pre-seeded to 0' then separately introduced a fifth (ScheduleRunner) metric without confirming its pre-seed status -- code confirms it IS pre-seeded identically (server.cpp), the ADR text was just incomplete, not wrong.
classification_rationale: incomplete, not contradictory
waiver_rationale: Fixed: added 'also pre-seeded to 0 at construction, same rationale as the four above' to the ScheduleRunner metric's sentence.

trigger: an exception escapes the per-connection scope in agent.cpp while stream is alive but STALLED (not dead -- gateway up, not draining), and keepalive_thread_ is at that moment blocked inside stream->Write(); the ScopeExit unwind guard's bare join() then blocks forever with no rescue
policy_floor: ownership/lifetime defect (unjoined/ambiguously-bounded thread join) -- CLAUDE.md cpp-safety policy floor
summary: keepalive_unwind_guard (added earlier this session to fix a UAF on the exception-escape path) called keepalive_stop_.store(true) then a bare, unbounded keepalive_thread_.join() with no context cancellation -- unlike the two other join sites (manual reconnect-teardown, quiesce_run_workers()), which are reached only after stream->Read() has already returned false, proving the connection dead. On the exception-unwind path the exception can land at ANY point, including while the stream is alive but merely stalled. This is the identical hazard class stop() already treats as cpp-safety BLOCKING for guardian_sink_stream_'s writer (a documented precedent a few hundred lines down in the same file): a synchronous Write() can wedge on a stalled-but-not-dead stream, and the established fix is TryCancel BEFORE the drain/join.
classification_rationale: the file's own documented fix pattern for this exact hazard class (cancel-before-join) was not applied to a second instance of the identical hazard
caused_by: an earlier fix round this same session (the ScopeExit UAF fix itself) -- introduced when closing one hazard without recognizing it shared shape with an already-documented sibling
waiver_rationale: Fixed: keepalive_unwind_guard now calls cancel_ctx(subscribe_ctx_) before join(), mirroring stop()'s own established pattern for the identical hazard on the same context. subscribe_ctx_ is still published at the point the guard runs (sub_slot retracts it only afterward), so the same rescue mechanism stop() uses is available and now used.

trigger: reading the queue-full erase comment against the actual absence of any in_flight_ids_ reset mechanism
summary: Comment claimed a skipped erase would leave the entry sitting 'until this agent's own reconnect-time reset' -- no such reset exists anywhere in the file (confirmed by grep, independently by both cpp-safety and architect). Harmless in practice (every actual exit path does erase correctly), but the comment asserted a nonexistent backstop, understating the real consequence (permanent leak until process exit).
classification_rationale: comment inaccuracy adjacent to correct code, not a control-flow defect
waiver_rationale: Fixed: comment corrected to state the true consequence (permanent leak, not reconnect-scoped) as the actual reason this erase is required.

trigger: Postgres pool exhaustion or a query failure inside claim_concurrency_slots (a fail-closed path)
summary: claim_concurrency_slots's two fail-closed early returns (pool exhaustion, query failure) excluded every candidate from dispatch, same as a genuinely-busy candidate, but incremented no metric -- an operator watching only yuzu_server_dispatch_concurrency_skipped_total couldn't distinguish real contention from store degradation.
classification_rationale: missing observability signal on a fail-closed path, no correctness impact
waiver_rationale: Fixed: added a new counter yuzu_server_concurrency_claim_unavailable_total, incremented at both fail-closed early-return sites, described()'d at server construction alongside the other five concurrency metrics, and documented in docs/user-manual/metrics.md and the ADR's metrics section.

trigger: future maintenance dropping or misordering the definition_id filter in renew_concurrency_claim's WHERE clause, with no test to catch the regression
summary: The Gate 2 cross-definition-leak regression test covered release_concurrency_claim and release_concurrency_claims but not the third sibling changed in the identical fix, renew_concurrency_claim -- the only test reaching it (the CHAOS-TTL-1 renewal test) uses a single definition_id throughout and cannot detect a dropped definition_id filter on the renewal path specifically. Current code was verified correctly scoped by direct read; this was a coverage gap, not a live bug.
classification_rationale: missing regression coverage for one of three functions fixed identically in the same round
waiver_rationale: Fixed: added a dedicated test ('renew_concurrency_claim does NOT touch a different definition's open claim when execution_id collides') that claims two definitions under the same collided execution_id, renews only one via a real reconciler pass timing check, and proves the other force-releases on schedule (i.e. was never touched by the renewal call).

trigger: a future change to discovery_routes.cpp's entra-sync-in-progress branch (status code, body shape, or the auth_fn/audit_fn wiring) shipping a regression with no test to catch it at the route layer
summary: The new 409 route mapping for a concurrent Entra sync (discovery_routes.cpp:105-113) is tested only at the store layer (test_directory_sync.cpp exercises sync_entra's return value) -- test_discovery_routes.cpp has zero references to entra/409/sync_entra, so a wrong status code or a broken audit call in the route-level branch would ship undetected.
classification_rationale: route-layer HTTP-mapping behavior has no test, only the underlying store method does
waiver_rationale: Deferred, not fixed in this round: a bounded-blast-radius test gap (this PR's own scope is concurrency enforcement, not DirectorySync route testing -- the 409 fix was itself a small bundled fix, not this PR's main deliverable). quality-engineer's suggested approach (reuse the existing test_hook_after_entra_guard_acquired_ determinism technique through TestRouteSink) is a reasonable follow-up. To be filed as a follow-up issue per the governance post-run procedure, alongside SEC-CLAIM-NO-LIFETIME-CEILING.

trigger: a reader trusting definition_id_for_execution's doc comment about its own call frequency
summary: definition_id_for_execution's doc comment claimed "Only called on a terminal transition, not per poll" -- contradicted by the running-branch call site, which fires on every ~5-minute keepalive tick per in-flight command, not just once at completion.
classification_rationale: comment-vs-code truth defect, no behavioral impact
waiver_rationale: Fixed: comment corrected to state it is called on every terminal transition AND every running/keepalive tick, with an accurate characterization of the per-tick cost (indexed PK lookup, not free, but negligible).

trigger: an operator or future maintainer reading first_response_at and assuming it always reflects the plugin's own first progress signal
summary: Keepalive RUNNING pings flow through notify_exec_tracker's normal RUNNING mapping, so they set first_response_at=now and publish an agent-transition SSE event for a command whose plugin has sent no real output yet -- an intended but previously undocumented consequence of the keepalive existing.
classification_rationale: undocumented side effect of a new mechanism on an existing field's semantics
waiver_rationale: Fixed: added a note in the ADR's CLOSED (agent-core keepalive) section clarifying the keepalive is SSE-silent only on the per-output-row stream, not the agent-transition event, and that first_response_at now usually reflects the keepalive's first tick for quiet long-running commands.

trigger: a server restart (or, routinely, any workflow-step dispatch) while a per-device-gated command is in flight, combined with cmd_execution_ids_ being a plain never-persisted in-memory map
summary: notify_exec_tracker silently dropped both keepalive renewals and the eventual real terminal response whenever cmd_execution_ids_ could not resolve execution_id, leaving the claim's expires_at frozen until the reconciler force-released it -- potentially while the agent was still genuinely executing, reopening the double-dispatch race this whole feature exists to prevent.
classification_rationale: a correctness-relevant control-flow gap in the claim lifecycle's release/renew path
waiver_rationale: Fixed: added a command_id-keyed fallback (release/renew_concurrency_claim_by_command) that notify_exec_tracker now uses whenever execution_id cannot be resolved. Hardened per independent adversarial review (Sol/Fable) with a real DB-enforced uniqueness constraint on (command_id, agent_id) and 128-bit generation. Regression tests added. Full server suite green (6018/6018, 111609/111609 assertions).

trigger: a reordered/redelivered running keepalive arriving after a real terminal write whose own release_concurrency_claim failed (pool blip, left the claim open)
summary: update_agent_status branched release-vs-renew on the caller-supplied s.status rather than the row's actually-persisted status, so a stale reordered running write could call renew_concurrency_claim and extend a dead command's claim even though the sticky-terminal CASE had already correctly kept the row terminal.
classification_rationale: decision branched on the wrong source of truth (caller input vs persisted state)
waiver_rationale: Fixed: upsert_agent_status_once now returns the actually-persisted status (std::optional<std::string> from its own RETURNING clause); update_agent_status gates release-vs-renew on that, never on the caller-supplied value. Regression test added proving the stale-running-after-terminal case now takes the release branch.

trigger: an extended PostgreSQL outage exceeding kConcurrencyReconcileBigStepFloorSeconds (1 hour) with several per-device claims mid-flight, followed by PG recovery
summary: Reported as an instantaneous mass-release the moment PG recovers; traced against the actual reconciler code and found already substantially mitigated by the existing big_step clock-guard anomaly (declines the first post-outage pass entirely) plus the unconditional 5000/pass release cap -- real residual is a one-tick delay then a capped, gradual drain, not an unbounded instant burst.
classification_rationale: existing clock-guard machinery already narrows this; not a newly introduced gap
waiver_rationale: Verified and documented rather than further hardened: the big_step decline and 5000-cap were built for exactly this class of event and predate this finding. No evidence the residual one-tick/capped-drain window is operationally material. Filed as a follow-up to revisit if it ever proves otherwise, per the ADR's Follow-ups section.

trigger: a tight retry loop (buggy or malicious agentic caller) dispatching against a persistently-unreachable agent, exploiting the cheap not_sent fast-release path
summary: No rate limit bounds claim+release cycles against one (definition_id, agent_id) pair, so a retry loop can append permanently-retained rows to concurrency_claims faster than the ADR's organic-dispatch-volume growth model assumed -- amplifies an already-accepted no-prune design rather than introducing a new failure mode.
classification_rationale: missing rate limit; growth-model assumption not accounting for pathological retry patterns
waiver_rationale: A rate limiter is materially larger scope than this ADR's enforcement mechanism. The existing no-prune design already accepts unbounded-but-slow growth as a deliberate tradeoff (Gate 6 compliance/sre reviewed); this just raises the assumed ceiling on growth rate. Filed as a follow-up to revisit alongside a future age-based prune pass.

trigger: two terminal CommandResponses with different outcomes (e.g. a redelivered failure after a success) arriving out of order for the same execution_id/agent_id
summary: The sticky-terminal CASE only special-cases terminal-over-terminal in one direction (blocks running from overwriting terminal); a second terminal write with a different outcome always overwrites, so completed_at/exit_code/error_detail can regress to an earlier wall-clock value with no sequence key to order by. Confirmed cosmetic only -- no dead-end state, no write ever permanently rejected.
classification_rationale: pre-existing, accepted design characteristic (HA WS-0 redelivery precedent already documented in the sticky-CASE's own comment)
waiver_rationale: Pre-existing behavior this PR did not introduce and the code's own comment already characterizes as intentional. A sequence/ordering key would be a real improvement but belongs to the general terminal-response-redelivery design, not a concurrency-claim-specific patch. Documented in the ADR's Gate 4 risk-register section.

trigger: unresolved -- reviewer could not name a concrete trigger beyond a narrow window on a single request thread
summary: claim_fn runs against a ContainmentGate quarantine snapshot taken earlier in the same call chain; a quarantine action landing in the gap between snapshot and claim INSERT could in principle let a claim be taken for a device quarantined moments before send. Strictly narrower than the ADR's already-documented 'quarantined mid-flight' residual gap.
classification_rationale: speculative -- no code path or concrete trigger nameable, only a hypothesis
waiver_rationale: Speculative epistemic status exempts this from gating per the governance framework (no code path or candidate trigger nameable). Documented in the ADR's Gate 4 risk-register section as a narrower instance of an already-accepted residual gap; no action taken.

trigger: a claim INSERT racing the reconciler's force-release UPDATE for the same row
summary: Verified-safe, not a defect: Postgres blocks the INSERT on the partial unique index until the reconciler's transaction resolves; a rollback yields only a transient, self-healing 'busy' report, never a double-claim.
classification_rationale: non-finding -- confirmed correct by reading the actual locking behavior
waiver_rationale: No action -- confirmed safe by design (DB-enforced serialization), not merely assumed. Noted in the ADR's Gate 4 risk-register section for completeness.

trigger: an attempt to craft agent_id/definition_id input to defeat ux_concurrency_claims_open
summary: Verified-safe, not a defect: agent_id/definition_id are server/registry-sourced, never free-form external input, and Postgres text handling rejects embedded NULs outright, failing the INSERT closed via existing error paths. No plausible collision bypassing the uniqueness constraint.
classification_rationale: non-finding -- confirmed correct by reading the actual insertion/input-provenance code
waiver_rationale: No action -- confirmed safe by design (input provenance + DB text handling), not merely assumed. Noted in the ADR's Gate 4 risk-register section for completeness.

trigger: any per-device command still executing past the 5-minute keepalive interval
summary: get_agent_statistics's success CASE (exit_code = 0 AND status != 'pending') and its WHERE clause (excluding only pending/dispatched) both let a genuinely in-flight 'running' row -- exit_code defaults to 0 on the wire until a real terminal response sets it -- count as a completed success. Pre-existing classifier gap, previously rare (only a plugin crossing the 64KB output-flush threshold); this PR's own agent-core keepalive makes it routine for every per-device dispatch running past 5 minutes.
classification_rationale: wrong-result classifier on a live REST-exposed statistics surface, materially amplified (not introduced) by this PR's own change
waiver_rationale: Fixed: 'running' added to the WHERE exclusion; success CASE tightened to explicit status = 'success' (also closes a previously-unreported latent timeout/failure double-count with exit_code=0); vestigial 'error' status value dropped from the failure CASE (never written anywhere). Regression test added. Full server suite green (verified via targeted execution_statistics/rest_api_t2/execution_tracker suites; full-suite run in progress at time of this ledger write).

trigger: N/A -- this is a test-design synthesis pass, not a finding
summary: Synthesized the Gate 4 unhappy-path risk register (UP-3 through UP-8, UP-1/UP-2 already closed) and consistency-auditor's CA-1 (already closed) into 7 chaos scenarios (CH-1 through CH-7) with success criteria and rollback procedures. Scope decision: nothing blocks push to origin -- every remaining finding derives SHOULD/NICE or speculative, none CRITICAL/HIGH, no policy floor. CH-1/CH-5 filed as new P1 issues (#3823, #3824); CH-2 filed as new P2 issue (#3825); CH-3/CH-4 attached as evidence-gathering comments to existing #3819/#3820; CH-6/CH-7 noted directly in the ADR, not filed separately (low severity, already-accepted disposition).
classification_rationale: test-design synthesis, not a code/doc defect classification
waiver_rationale: Gate 5 complete. All actionable scenarios filed as tracked backlog (issues #3823, #3824, #3825) or attached to existing issues (#3819, #3820) or documented in the ADR (CH-6, CH-7). No scenario derived a merge-blocking severity.

trigger: an operator or integrator reading upgrading.md/instructions.md/yaml-dsl-spec.md for workflow-step claim-release timing, after the UP-1/UP-2 fix landed in the same PR
summary: Three operator-facing docs still claimed workflow-step per-device claims were release-by-TTL-only after the by-command fallback fix (this same PR) made that false -- self-inflicted contradiction against the ADR's own already-corrected section. Independently found by sre (Finding D) in the same Gate 6 wave.
classification_rationale: stale doc-truth defect, domain fact contradicted by the PR's own code change
waiver_rationale: Fixed: all three files (upgrading.md, instructions.md, yaml-dsl-spec.md) corrected to state workflow-step claims release-on-terminal-response/renew-on-keepalive like any other path, with the unaffected executions-drawer correlation gap called out separately so the two aren't conflated. Also fixed a matching stale ADR Follow-ups bullet (sre's independent catch) that still cited the closed section as an open item.

trigger: an Administrator/PlatformEngineer opens the Form-mode instruction editor for one of the 21 definitions using concurrency_mode=global/global-singleton and clicks Save
summary: The Concurrency Mode <select> offers only 4 options (unlimited/per-device/per-definition/per-set); a real, shipped 5th/6th value (global/global-singleton, 21 definitions) never matches, so the browser silently defaults to displaying Unlimited, and Convert-to-YAML + Save bakes that wrong default in, silently overwriting the definition's real concurrency_mode. Pre-existing (this PR did not change the option list/matching logic), not mechanically amplified by this PR's diff -- but derives HIGH by the same strict rules as every other finding in this review, and the fix was cheap enough to make in-round rather than defer (matching the fix-vs-defer bar this session has applied throughout, not a silent downgrade of the derived band).
classification_rationale: silent data corruption on an ordinary UI save action, pre-existing but newly discovered via this PR's own real-usage audit
waiver_rationale: Fixed: a fifth, dynamically-emitted <option> now carries the actual stored value (selected) whenever it doesn't match one of the four known modes, in both the edit-prefill and new-definition-clear code paths. No regression test added (this whole route has zero pre-existing test coverage of any kind; building route-level test infra from scratch was judged disproportionate to this one fix) -- verified by direct code trace and clean compile only.

trigger: an operator scanning upgrading.md by its own established grep-for-warning-emoji convention
summary: Claimed the ADR-1007 section header was missing a supposedly-universal warning-emoji convention shared by all Breaking/Behaviour-change headers in the file.
classification_rationale: verified FALSE on cross-check -- warning emoji is reserved for Breaking/Security-labeled headers specifically (5 of them); ordinary Behaviour-change headers (20 of them) never carry it, and this entry is correctly classified as Behaviour change, not Breaking
waiver_rationale: Verified against the actual file before acting (claim-discipline check): the reviewer's premise was wrong -- adding the emoji would have violated the real convention, not followed it. No change made.

trigger: a repeating/alternating clock anomaly causing sustained reconciler declines, or the liveness gauge going stale, with no alert wired; or an operator needing to triage a wedged reconciler with no runbook
summary: The concurrency-claims reconciler shares its clock-guard decision rule with audit_store's and rotation-sweep's reconcilers, both of which ship a full alert family + ops runbook for the identical shared mechanism; this one ships neither, nor a current-open/stale-claim gauge despite the counts already being computed for free on every pass. Three findings (A/B/C in the raw report) consolidated into one issue per this repo's dedupe convention.
classification_rationale: observability parity gap against two direct architectural siblings using the identical shared mechanism
waiver_rationale: Deferred: building a full gauge+alert-family+runbook package is a real, proportionate scope of work but larger than a fix-in-round item, matching how this session has handled every other MEDIUM finding of this shape (UP-3, UP-4, SEC-CLAIM-NO-LIFETIME-CEILING, QE-DIRECTORYSYNC-409-ROUTE-UNTESTED). Filed as one consolidated issue per sre's own explicit recommendation.

trigger: a per-device command dispatched to an agent still on a pre-this-release build during a staged rolling upgrade (server upgraded first, per the standing mandatory-order rule), running long enough and quietly enough to approach the claim's TTL ceiling
summary: The keepalive that closes CHAOS-TTL-1 lives in the agent binary; an old agent during a rolling upgrade has no keepalive thread, so a long quiet command on it remains exposed to the same race CHAOS-TTL-1 was raised to close. This PR strictly NARROWS a pre-existing exposure (old agents were always at risk; new agents are now protected) -- it does not widen anything -- but the upgrade doc stated 'No operator action is required' with no version-dependency caveat, unlike this same file's own established template for exactly this shape of gap (the fleet-viz PR-12 rolling-upgrade-behaviour row).
classification_rationale: undocumented rolling-upgrade residual, using this repo's own established doc template as the bar
waiver_rationale: Fixed: added a Rolling-upgrade behaviour paragraph to upgrading.md's ADR-1007 section, matching the file's own fleet-viz PR-12 template sentence shape, stating plainly that this is a narrowing of a pre-existing exposure, not a new one, and pointing at the mandatory server-first upgrade order.

trigger: a future regression silently stops one of the six new metrics from firing
summary: test_execution_tracker.cpp never wires a MetricsRegistry, unlike its sibling test_audit_store.cpp, which does assert on its own clock-guard metrics -- a latent CI-coverage gap for a future regression, explicitly not raised as a standalone actionable finding by the reporting agent.
classification_rationale: latent test-coverage gap, reporter explicitly framed this as non-actionable-standalone
waiver_rationale: Reporting agent explicitly characterized this as an addendum, not a standalone finding requiring action ('not a present defect'). No action taken; folded conceptually into the scope of issue #3830 if that work ever wires metric assertions, but not a required acceptance criterion there.

trigger: an operator reading release notes for GET /api/v1/execution-statistics/agents's reported numbers after upgrading
summary: The changelog fragment never mentioned the get_agent_statistics fix (commit 1fe958a29) despite it materially changing a REST-visible surface's reported success/failure counts.
classification_rationale: missing changelog coverage for an operator-visible behavior change, per this repo's own changelog policy rule 3
waiver_rationale: Fixed: added a bullet to the existing fragment describing the statistics fix.

trigger: an investigator later trying to determine whether a specific claim release was a normal terminal response or a force-release, from the store alone, without log retention
summary: Force-released and normally-released claims are indistinguishable in the durable concurrency_claims row -- both just set released_at, no release_reason column. The reconciler's spdlog::warn line is the only signal and isn't queryable audit evidence.
classification_rationale: evidentiary-completeness gap on a new, still-unshipped table -- reporting agent explicitly framed as not required to merge
waiver_rationale: Not fixed in this round per the reporting agent's own explicit 'not required to merge' framing -- an evidentiary-completeness improvement, not a control failure, the mechanism functions correctly either way. Noted in the ADR's Retention section as a candidate for the same future round that builds the age-based prune pass, since a schema column addition is cheaper now (zero production rows) than later.

trigger: a future auditor reconstructing every finding raised against this PR from the ledger alone, without also reading the ADR
summary: The Sol/Fable adversarial-review findings (command_id collision-safety, empty-command_id claim-side asymmetry) live only in ADR prose and code comments, not as their own ledger rows in either governance ledger file -- a record-location gap, not a record-absence gap (the evidence trail exists, just split). Also noted: several rows carry a non-reproducible reviewed_at_sha placeholder, and the sibling ledger file's internal run_id doesn't match its own filename.
classification_rationale: ledger completeness/housekeeping, explicitly framed as non-blocking informational by the reporting agent
waiver_rationale: Partially remediated: added retroactive ledger rows (this pass) recording the Sol/Fable adversarial-review findings and their fix dispositions, closing the record-location gap for future auditors relying on the ledger alone. The reviewed_at_sha/run_id-filename housekeeping items in the OTHER ledger file (3784-concurrency-review-fixes.oFqHzY.jsonl, from an earlier session) are cosmetic and left as-is per the reporting agent's own 'doesn't affect usability today' framing.

trigger: a future code path reusing a command_id for the same agent across two different definitions -- not reachable in code as it existed at review time, but structurally unconstrained
summary: Independent adversarial review (Sol/gpt-5.6-sol, opine mode, consulted ahead of formal Gate 4) of the UP-1/UP-2 fix found command_id's uniqueness was probabilistic (8 random bytes = 64 bits) and completely unenforced at the DB level -- a doc comment claiming the (command_id, agent_id) match key 'cannot collide' was an overclaim the schema didn't back up. No reachable trigger found in code as it existed, but the by-command release/renew mechanism's entire safety argument rested on this unenforced assumption.
classification_rationale: unenforced structural safety assumption backing a new claim-release match key
